findings.title: On the development reference the frozen rules cannot reach the low end of O004's registration span
findings.detail: O004 requires the registered L1 ratios to span at least [0.75, 0.98], with at least 3 below 0.90. On 2D_Case_4 the module's own findings are: best single move 0.873, lowest compound found 0.7616. The test `test_case4_low_ratio_pair` encodes this as a strict xfail, so it is disclosed and not hidden. The four move rules are implemented and DRC-gated, but the frozen rules as delivered are not shown to produce a registrable design. The claim holds only as 'the rules are implemented', not 'the rules are sufficient for O004'.
findings.evidence: tests/unit/test_perturb.py: test_case4_low_ratio_pair is marked xfail(strict=True); LOWEST_COMPOUND r=0.7616; O004 objective.yaml scope_in requires the span [0.75, 0.98].
findings.suggested_check: Founder decision (I0217) on the span or the ranges before E004 registration.

findings.title: rules_sha256 does not cover every input that decides which layouts a seed yields
findings.detail: The docstring says the hash covers 'everything that decides which layouts a seed yields', but several imported inputs are not hashed: the NETS tuple, whose order `_draw_params` indexes with the rng for trace_width and terminal_copper; SIGNAL_NET and SIGNAL_PADS, which the DRC uses; Die.box; BondWire.length and SignalWire.length (the DRC wire-length checks); and the shapely/numpy versions. A change to NETS order in geometry/layout.py would change the draws for a sealed seed without changing the hash.
findings.evidence: Scratch probe: after `P.NETS = tuple(reversed(P.NETS))` the hash is unchanged (True); after emptying `drc.rules.SIGNAL_NET` it is also unchanged (True).
findings.suggested_check: Add NETS/SIGNAL_NET/SIGNAL_PADS to the hashed names, add the sources of Die.box and BondWire.length, or pin the commit in E004's spec.

findings.title: 'Long side' depends on the polygon's vertex list, not its geometry
findings.detail: `long_sides` splits edges at collinear vertices. The set of trace_width edges therefore depends on how the reference polygon was built. Any earlier move that passes a net through `_set_net` (which canonicalizes it) changes the edge set for the same geometry. Example: Case 4 PHASE edge 0 is ('h',30,25,55) on the reference but ('h',30,25,65) once PHASE has been canonicalized, e.g. by an LS die-row shift in a compound. 2D_Case_2R PHASE and 2D_Case_6 PHASE/DC+ show the same split edges. When only part of a geometric edge is widened, the copper gets a step rather than a uniform width change. The behaviour is deterministic and DRC-gated, so this is not a correctness failure.
findings.evidence: Case 4 PHASE raw long_sides [('h',30,25,55),...] vs canonical [('h',30,25,65),...]. 2R PHASE raw ('h',15,7,37),('v',47,15,47) vs canonical ('h',15,7,47),('v',47,15,51). Case 6 PHASE raw has 6 h-sides, canonical has 4.
findings.suggested_check: Compute long_sides on `_canonical(poly)`, or state the representation dependence in the frozen rule text.

findings.title: The whole-mm construction is absolute, not relative to l2_layout's lattice origin
findings.detail: `_mm` rounds absolute coordinates with Python's round-half-to-even (10.5 mm -> 10, 11.5 mm -> 12). l2_layout's lattice origin is the bounding-box minimum of the baseplate and the copper. The docstring says 'a reference on l2_layout's 1 mm lattice stays on the 1.0/0.5/0.25 mm lattices', but that holds only when the lattice origin is at whole mm. `draw` does not check on_lattice. All three references have whole-mm copper coordinates, so the current use is unaffected.
findings.evidence: Probe: round(10.5)=10, round(11.5)=12, P._mm(10.5e-3)=10. Case 4, 2R and Case 6 power polygons are all at whole mm, and Case 4 dies are 4x6 mm centred at whole mm.
findings.suggested_check: Have `draw`/`measured_rules` assert that the reference coordinates are whole mm, or reject draws that fail on_lattice.

findings.title: The test of positive terminal_copper is vacuous
findings.detail: In `test_terminal_copper_declared_changes_closed_form`, the 'grown' case (PHASE, S, margin 0, delta +2) places its slab at y 65..67, x 57..60. That lies inside the existing PHASE column (x 55..65), so the copper does not change. The `>=` area assertion passes trivially. No closed-form test covers a positive slab that actually adds copper.
findings.evidence: PHASE terminal is 3x3 mm at (58.5, 68.5) and the PHASE polygon includes x 55..65, y 60..98 (from the printed Case 4 geometry).
findings.suggested_check: Add a positive-delta case whose slab leaves the copper, with a closed-form area gain.

findings.title: Compound pair kind is beyond the four stated moves and its authorisation is not in the repo
findings.detail: The claim lists four moves. The module also adds a fifth pair kind, 'compound', citing founder guidance I0217. I0217 does not appear anywhere in project/ at this commit, so I could not verify the authorisation. The compound does not alter the single moves: the test shows that the single draws for a seed are unchanged when compounds are added.
findings.evidence: grep -r I0217 project/ finds nothing; it appears only in the packet.

findings.title: Unit test draws development-seed geometry on the judged references
findings.detail: `test_geometry_only_on_2r_and_case6` draws all move kinds on 2D_Case_2R and 2D_Case_6 (seed 7) and asserts they are DRC-clean and on the lattice. No inductance is computed, and it guards against that. Still, the rules' success on the judged geometry is checked before registration, while F2 says development work uses 2D_Case_4 and development seeds only.

independent_checks_performed: Ran `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_perturb.py`: 43 passed, 1 xfailed (strict) in 14.7 s. Ran `uv run ruff check` on both deliverables: all checks passed.

Read drc/rules.py `check` to confirm that `draw`'s DRC gate actually catches the failure modes the moves can create: die off its host or wrong net, die edge margin, net split, spacing, edge margin, wire landing on the wrong net or off copper, landing keep-out, wire start on pad, wire length and pitch, signal wire landing and bondability, terminal off its copper.

Printed the Case 4 reference geometry (dies 4x6 mm at whole-mm centres, terminals, all polygons at whole mm) and the 2R/Case 6 power polygons. All coordinates are whole mm, so absolute whole-mm moves stay on l2_layout's lattice for these references.
Read l2_layout.layout_lattice: the lattice origin is the bounding-box minimum of the baseplate and copper, CELL[0] defaults to 0.5 mm, and on_lattice overrides it.
Compared long_sides on raw vs canonical polygons for Case 4 PHASE, 2R PHASE and Case 6 PHASE/DC+. The edge sets differ, so the result depends on the vertex list.
Probed rules_sha256 coverage: reversing P.NETS and emptying drc.rules.SIGNAL_NET both leave the hash unchanged.
Probed `_mm` rounding: round half to even (10.5 -> 10, 11.5 -> 12).

Hand-checked the declared side effects of die_row_shift (pads and wire starts move by (dx,dy), landings by the along-row part, host copper grown by enc_mm around whole-mm die bounds) and of terminal_copper (slab geometry against the window) against the code.

Checked test independence: die_row_shift and trace_width are compared with O006's independently built 'die_shift' and 'trace_width' variants, and the areas are closed-form. Found the positive terminal_copper assertion vacuous by hand from the Case 4 geometry.
caveats: The permission layer refused several of my scratch scripts that called `draw` or DRC `check` on extra seeds, and one that translated the reference by 0.5 mm. So I did not independently sweep extra seeds or build the half-mm-offset adversarial reference. Draw-level lattice and DRC cleanliness rest on the author's tests (seeds 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12) plus my reading of the code.
The rules are shown only for references whose copper, dies and baseplate lie at absolute whole mm, with one die row per switch and exactly one trace per power net.
The frozen rules do not reach r <= 0.75 on the development reference. Whether O004's registration span is achievable is an open founder decision, not something this change establishes.
I could not verify I0217, which the compound pair kind depends on, from the repository at this commit.
